bull.t: Strong and growing free cash flow
bull.b: DoorDash’s expanding free cash flow shows that recent profitability is translating into substantial cash rather than remaining purely accounting-based. This supports continued investment in technology, fulfillment, merchant tools and international growth while preserving flexibility for future capital allocation.

bull.t: Broad platform growth across memberships and new verticals
bull.b: Growth is becoming more diversified beyond restaurant delivery as membership, grocery and other local-commerce categories gain traction. Higher subscription penetration, rising basket sizes and order frequency can deepen customer engagement and improve gross profit per user over time.

DoorDash is strengthening its ecosystem on both sides of the marketplace through merchant software and international scale. Growing merchant-services adoption can improve retention and order frequency, while Deliveroo’s improving economics broadens the platform’s durable global growth opportunity.

bear.t: Modest margins and slowing revenue growth
bear.b: Although DoorDash has reached profitability, its operating and net margins remain modest for a scaled platform, leaving earnings sensitive to delivery costs and execution. Slower growth than earlier periods could also make margin expansion more important to sustaining future profit growth.

Moderate leverage remains manageable, but the sharp increase from prior years reduces some financial flexibility. If growth slows or margins compress, higher debt relative to equity could increase pressure on cash allocation and make investment decisions more constrained.

bear.t: Complex execution risk from major infrastructure initiatives
bear.b: DoorDash is pursuing several complex initiatives simultaneously, including autonomy, fulfillment and a unified technology stack. These programs may improve cost and service quality, but their operational complexity creates timing and execution risk that could delay expected benefits or absorb management attention.
